title: Bartholomew's Berry Pies
markdown:
Sunbeams danced through the leaves of Whisperwood Meadow, as they always do on a lovely morning. Clementine the fawn twitched her velvety ears. Her dappled coat looked like a sprinkle of tiny brown stars, and her eyes were as deep and calm as a quiet pond.

Beside her, Wren the robin bobbed his plump red-and-brown self until his whole body swayed. His bright quick eyes noticed everything — a shiny dewdrop on a silken thread, the tippy-top of the tallest oak.

Not far away, nestled among mossy stones, Mr Tinker the badger hummed a rumbling tune. He was polishing a smooth grey stone, finding a happy quietness in making it gleam. Gentle breezes moved. Little sounds ticked and chirped. It was a day as bright as a painted picture.

Over by a patch of sunshine-yellow daisies, a very busy mole named Bartholomew Buttercup had a grand idea. Bartholomew was good at digging tunnels, as moles are. He also loved to make things — to shape and colour and create.

Today he was making a sign. He dipped his tiny brush into a pot of bright berry juice. It stained his paws a delightful vibrant purple. With a steady paw he painted large cheerful letters: Fresh Pies Today. He added swirls and dots like tiny happy dancers. At the bottom he painted a plump red strawberry with green leaves. He hung the sign from a sturdy twig outside his burrow, and imagined happy visitors smelling his pies and coming to say hello.

Clementine and Wren and Mr Tinker happened to be strolling by just as Bartholomew finished the very last dot. Clementine stopped, her soft fawn legs still.

“Oh, my. Look how pretty that sign is, Wren. It’s like a rainbow on a stick.”

Wren darted over and landed on a nearby buttercup. “Chirp, chirp. Such lovely colours.”

Mr Tinker peered over spectacles perched comically on his striped nose. “Indeed. Bartholomew has a real artist’s touch. That sign is a masterpiece.”

Bartholomew peeked from his burrow, his little mole eyes blinking in the sunlight. He beamed. His whiskers wiggled, and a warmth spread through his little body, making him feel as bright as the sunbeam warming his fur.

As more little creatures ambled along the meadow path, their eyes went to the artwork, not to the promise of pies. A family of rabbits paused. Mama Rabbit nudged her little ones closer.

“My, my. What a charming sign.”

A busy squirrel with a tail as bushy as a feather duster scampered down an oak. “It’s the prettiest sign I’ve ever seen.”

Everyone spoke of the berry-red paint, the neat round letters that looked like little smiles, and the cheerful strawberry painted with such care. They nodded. They smiled. They walked on, minds filled with the beauty of the sign, forgetting to peek inside for a pie.

Bartholomew looked a little puzzled. His whiskers drooped. A tiny sigh escaped him. He had the prettiest sign in the meadow, and no one was coming to his door.

Mr Tinker saw the quiet confusion. He remembered the wonderfully sweet smell of warm berry pie that had wafted out earlier. He tapped his chin with a thoughtful claw.

“A sign can be a wonderful thing. It can catch the eye and bring a smile. It is even better when it helps us find something equally wonderful.” He turned to Clementine and Wren. “Perhaps we could help Bartholomew show everyone that his pies are as delightful as his painting. What’s a beautiful song without anyone to listen?”

Clementine’s gentle eyes lit. “Oh, yes. We can help.”

Wren chirped, “I can fly ahead and tell everyone Bartholomew’s pies are extra yummy today. The very best pies in all of Whisperwood.”

So Wren zipped through the meadow, red breast a flash against the green. “The pies are as sweet as the sign is pretty.”

Clementine nudged a few curious noses toward the burrow. “Do try a little bit,” she whispered to a passing field mouse. “You won’t be disappointed.”

Bartholomew, feeling a little braver, offered a tiny warm berry pie sample on a wide green leaf. The first to taste it was a busy bee returning to its hive. It took a tiny bite. Sweetness, warm and comforting, tickled its antennae. It closed its eyes and buzzed with delight.

“This pie is even more delicious than the sign is beautiful. It tastes like sunshine and berries all mixed together.”

Soon, the path was bustling again, but this time with creatures eager for a taste of Bartholomew’s wonderful pies. Laughter and happy munching sounds filled the air, and Bartholomew Buttercup’s burrow was filled with cheerful visitors. The beautiful sign and the yummy pies made a perfect pair, like a lovely song sung by a cheerful bird. Bartholomew watched his friends, his heart full and warm, feeling like the happiest little mole in Whisperwood. The berry juice on his paws had dried to a proud purple, and the sign still hung from its sturdy twig, strawberry and all.
characters: Clementine (a dappled meadow fawn), Wren (a red-breasted robin), Mr. Tinker (a stone-polishing badger)
author: StoryGen Community
